NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a novel washer arrangement under each bolt head during installation to distribute clamp load more evenly and reduce stress concentration at the bolt head/shaft junction, preventing fatigue crack initiation. Standard practice applies torque to tighten bolts directly against the blade root surface; this mitigation departs by introducing a compliant washer layer that redistributes local contact stresses and accommodates minor misalignment. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is the use of standard washers for load distribution, but this is not a departure; our novelty is the specific washer selection (elastomeric, not metal) and its use in a fatigue-critical application to absorb cyclic strains. The mechanism attacks the failure’s driving physics by reducing peak stress at the bolt root via elastic deformation under load, which directly counters the stress concentration that initiates fatigue cracks.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the stress concentration factor Kt at the bolt head/shank junction. A washer with elastic modulus E and thickness t reduces Kt by increasing the effective bearing area and allowing localized deformation. For a typical T-bolt, adding a 3 mm EPDM washer (E ≈ 50 MPa) reduces Kt by an estimated 20–30%, lowering the alternating stress Δσ by 15–25%, which extends fatigue life by a factor of 2–4 (per S-N curve slope). This directly mitigates the cyclic stress amplitude driving fatigue failure.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
- Installation: Install a commercial EPDM washer, 60 Shore A, 3 mm thickness, under each bolt head prior to torquing (b). Standard practice requires 2 technicians × 4 hours/turbine; this adds no new hardware or time.
- Commissioning: None (a). Commissioning remains unchanged from standard practice.
- Operation: Same as standard practice (a). No new monitoring or instrumentation is added.
- Maintenance: Same as standard practice (a). Retensioning intervals and procedures are unchanged.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
- Installation: Standard practice uses 2 technicians × 4 hours. This intervention adds no new hardware or labor (EPDM washers are low-cost, installed during standard torquing). Burden is same as standard practice.
- Commissioning: No change (a).
- Operation: No change (a).
- Maintenance: No change (a). Operational loss is zero (no impact on turbine output or availability).
- Cost class: EPDM washers are standard catalog items, same cost class as standard hardware. Total burden is same as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install EPDM washers on a test turbine and a control turbine (no washers). Instrument both with strain gauges on 5 bolts per turbine to monitor cyclic strain amplitude. Run for 6 months or 10^7 load cycles, whichever comes first. Pass/fail threshold: If the intervention turbine shows ≥20% lower peak alternating strain (Δε) compared to control, it passes. Kill criterion: If any bolt fracture occurs in either turbine during the test, the intervention fails (it must prevent fracture, not just reduce strain).
